internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The 13 occurrences divide into one return verb, three dialogue tokens, five proper/group designations for the disciples, and four hur nouns. Proposed cores based on returning, whiteness, or reciprocal exchange do not cover all four families distinctively.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Forms III/VI identify reciprocal dialogue, while surface families separate hawariyyun and hur. Morphology exposes the split but does not license an external derivation for the names.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The hur nouns in garden contexts have no return/dialogue role, and the hawariyyun group name is not semantically decomposed by its verses.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Returning/exchange links dialogue and return, while purity/whiteness links the two noun families; combining both is a two-core patch, not one root contribution.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: No candidate survived comparison without becoming a disjunction of lexical families.
internal_discovery.rationale: Complete coverage exposes four disconnected families; semantic unity is not forced.
